title: Who could read in 1830s France
hook: Can one average describe all of France?

doesNotKnow: how sharp the 1830s literacy split was: north and east about twice the south, west and centre

misconception: A national average describes most of the country.
objective: The learner can say that in Guerry's 1830s figures the north and east of France averaged about 55% of conscripts who could read and write against about 28% in the south, west and centre, so the 39% average across departments described neither half.

claims.text: Around the 1830s (Guerry 1833), the share of army conscripts who could read and write in each of France's 86 departments, and Guerry's region for each (north, east, south, west, centre; Corse has none).

recall.question: A country's average literacy is 50%: half its regions are at 80%, half at 20%. What does the average hide?
recall.why: No region is anywhere near 50%: the average sits between two very different halves and describes neither.
